budget.rationale: The published budget, unreduced. Each iteration asks the model once per island for each searched target; the roster's eight cells have eleven targets, so two seeds make 22 searches and 200 x 4 x 22 = 17,600 requests, each with upstream's 1,024-token output limit. In the smokes on 2026-10-18 (every cell, 20 iterations), 46 of the 880 replies to the prompt with the description reached that limit, 43 of them in the two detention cells, and 7 of the 880 to the published prompt; 30 of the 53 had written their three equations first, so about 2% of the description campaign's proposed equations were lost. The limit stays upstream's, decided on 2026-10-21. An iteration took 9 to 15 seconds for each target searched, so a search takes about 30 to 95 minutes.

prompt_policy.description: As published, decided on 2026-10-17 as a second campaign beside the one given the task description. LLM-ODE's prompt names the variables x_0 to x_n and describes neither them nor the system, as its paper withholds variable meanings and system descriptions to limit recall of memorized equations (Sec. 4.1).

scope_note: The eight Phase C roster cells with two seeds. LLM-ODE's own search at its published settings: 200 iterations, 4 islands of 2 programs, 8 examples and 3 new equations per prompt, the islands trimmed and mixed every 5 iterations, and upstream's 1,024-token output limit; no temperature or reasoning effort is sent, as upstream sends none, and the repetitions are unseeded, as upstream's are. One search per target: the supplied channels (auxiliaries, measured inputs and fixed covariates) are variables every equation may use, and only the targets are searched. Each trajectory is differentiated on its own, at fourth order as upstream does, and the rows are stacked. The system is chosen by the rule in the released code (system_selection). Given the prompt as published (prompt_policy).

system_selection.rationale: The rule in LLM-ODE's released code, decided on 2026-10-17. Their driver (llmode.LlmOde._store_results at 31667d9) scores every system in the product of the per-variable Pareto frontiers by the mean squared error, in the data's own units, of a rollout from the training initial state over the whole training trajectory (t from 0 to 10: the half its equations were fitted on and the half it validates on), sorts on it, and lists the test error beside it without using it. Here the rollout covers every development trajectory, training and validation (16 and 4, or 6 and 3 in the basin cells), each from its own first values, with the shared evaluator's solver (RK45, rtol 1e-7, atol 1e-9) and the supplied channels held to their observations; the targets' squared errors are pooled over every trajectory and time point. In the two- and three-target cells a target with larger values counts for more, as upstream's variables do. The paper's rule (Eq. 2, the knee of the systems' complexity-error front subject to T >= h * T_max with h = 0.1 and T = -MSE) is not in the released code, and as written it cannot be met: with T <= 0 it asks for an error below a tenth of the best. Upstream gives each rollout 2 seconds, with looser tolerances, on 100-point trajectories; here a rollout may take 30 seconds per trajectory, a tenth of the frozen evaluator's 300, and a system whose rollout fails or takes longer cannot be chosen, as there. The product is scored whole, as upstream has no cap. A system whose squared errors so far already exceed the lowest error a system has finished with is stopped there, which changes no choice. Eight processes score the systems, where upstream uses 30, and a tie goes to the first system in product order, best derivative fits first.
